reason: The translation uses Ruff's Python parser (`py_parses`) and its trivia-skipping tokenizer (`py_consecutive_names`) instead of the old bounded regex grammar, so the prose comments it accepted (`# SIM103 (but not fixable)`, `# (See: http://example.test/revision)`) are gone: fixtures 82 shared findings, none on one side only. Its 238 samples-python findings equal Ruff 0.17.6's exactly. The 6 translation-only keys are the quoted-attribute annotation comment `'month'. Eg: "Title must be unique for pub_date year"` in six Django samples (fields/__init__.py:150), which Ruff reports and the JSON original misses.

For `response_model=List[Item,]` versus `-> List[Item]`, Ruff reports FAST001 and so does the translation; the JSON original does not. Ruff treats the trailing subscript comma as insignificant when comparing these types.
